title_he: אֶקְדִּישׁ לַאדֹנִי יֵשׁוּעַ תּוֹדָתִי וְשִׁבְחִי בְּהַכְנָעָה
review: The hymn is Ps 103:2 (בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי … וְאַל־תִּשְׁכְּחִי כָּל־גְּמוּלָיו) turned into testimony: stanza 1 asks to be led, stanza 2 offers praise with a sacrifice's submission, and stanza 3 counts the rescues. 3:5–8 is Ps 107:6,13–14 and Isa 55:12.

1:1–2 is the printed two-long-line stanza; the Arabic يَا مَنْبَعَ الْحَنَان يَا مَصْدَرَ الْإِحْسَان is not a couplet the rest repeats, so the Hebrew keeps two lines and does not break them into the eight short lines of the following stanzas.

2:6 בַּיְּקוּם — the Arabic فِي الْوُجُود is 'in existence'; biblical Hebrew has no noun for the created order as a whole, so the line uses יְקוּם (Gen 7:4, כָּל־הַיְקוּם), the fixed term for all that exists. 2:8 שֶׁפַע עַל־שֶׁפַע renders جُودٌ فَوْقَ جُود with the same doubling.

3:2 אֲדֹנַיִךְ — the Arabic رَبُّكِ is feminine-suffixed because the soul is addressed as a woman throughout ('O soul'); the Hebrew keeps the second-person feminine singular in every vocative (נַפְשִׁי … הִצִּילֵךְ … הֱבִיאוּךְ), so the stanza reads as one address and not as a mixed one.

3:4 הֱבִיאוּךְ אֶל־מֶרְחָב רַב — the Arabic أَفْضَتْ إِلَى رَحْبٍ عَظِيم is 'led out into a wide place'; מֶרְחָב is the psalm's word for the open space of deliverance (Ps 18:20, וַיּוֹצִיאֵנִי לַמֶּרְחָב), and the plural subject (the straits) is kept from the Arabic.
